messages:
Mira: opened a tiny migration PR to clarify SOC2 wording around exports and add a compact client-side pseudonymization example (py + js). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1457

docs-bot: CI: docs build failed on staging - invalid code fence in exports/overview.md (line 78).

Omar: noted. Also saw the residency anchor moved in the refactor; will update links to #data-sovereignty. For the wording, should we say "may contain pseudonymized identifiers" or "can include pseudonymized tokens"?

Legal-Bot: Recommend: "Exported audit records can include pseudonymized tokens produced using customer-controlled salts or keys; re-identification requires possession of those salts/keys and is not performed by Redwood unless customers explicitly share keys." Keep it concise for SOC2 reviewers.

Mira: thanks. will adopt that exact sentence and add a short pointer to the key-management guidance page. Also replacing the python example that caused the fence error. New py sample (pseudocode):

```python
import hmac, hashlib
# get_customer_key is pseudocode - keys should be customer-managed (KMS/HSM)
key = get_customer_key(customer_id)

def pseudonymize(id_str):
    return hmac.new(key, id_str.encode('utf-8'), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
```

Mira: adding a terser JS example too using SubtleCrypto HMAC and noting it is for client-side pseudonymization only.

CLI-Checker: quick lint: please add a one-line changelog entry under docs/changelog.md -> Security: clarify export pseudonymization language and add client examples.

Omar: fixed the anchor and the broken fence, pushed changes. CI queued.

docs-bot: CI: build passed on staging - linkcheck ok, code-sample-check ok.

Mira: :rocket: merging in 10 unless any objections. Thanks all for quick turnaround.
